attempts.summary: Implemented the cross-LAN firewall using Ansible from the pre-provisioned control node (node4). node1 (VyOS) routes between lan-a (node2, 10.50.50.0/24, eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.60.60.0/24, eth2). An Ansible playbook (/root/cross-lan-firewall/site.yml on node4) configures: (1) static IPs + cross-LAN routes on node2/node3 via raw module (RHEL7 has no compatible Python for standard modules), (2) VyOS interface addresses and a forward-filter firewall on node1 (rule 10 accept established/related, rule 20 accept tcp/5432 lan-a->lan-b, rule 30 reject remaining lan-a->lan-b, rule 40 reject lan-b->lan-a), and (3) a firewalld rich rule on node3 permitting only 10.50.50.0/24 on tcp/5432 (the RHEL7 host firewall was itself blocking the allowed flow until this was added). Verified end-to-end: node2->node3:5432 succeeds; node2->node3:22 and ICMP are rejected (TCP RST / ICMP unreachable from node1); node3-initiated connections to node2 are rejected. All four managed nodes (node1-4) were restarted one at a time with baseline capture, boot-id change proof, and post-restart functional re-verification; configuration and playbook state persisted across all restarts and full functionality was re-confirmed on the last pass.
